findings.reason: the node must add coordinator-reference.md and AGENTS.md (or move these two edits to §2, which already writes both) or its stated migration is only partly done and its delivery is judged complete at the wrong scope.
findings.text: §6 states "every reckon caller that sets one moves to `close` in the same node", yet `skills/reckon-build/references/coordinator-reference.md:1103` ("Do not set `status` to `shipped` or `done`…") and `AGENTS.md:258` ("`status` updated (`active` → `shipped`/`done`…)") both instruct setting a terminal status and are absent from §6's declared write paths (`reckon/_store.py`, `reckon/_store_section_ops.py`, `reckon/mcp.py`, `skills/reckon-edit/SKILL.md`, `skills/reckon-build/SKILL.md`, tests) — so a node dispatched on those paths leaves the two instructions intact and a coordinator following them meets the new refusal with no path to `close`, the exact "caller that does not move" defect §6 claims to retire.

findings.reason: once the lead locks `deferred-continuation`, §8 becomes dispatchable with no edge holding it behind §7, so roadmap can rank it ready and run it concurrently on the same files the ordered chain writes.
findings.text: `plan-section-depends-on` orders §4←§2,§3; §5←§4; §6←§5; §7←§6, but declares no edge for §8, though §8's write paths include `reckon/_store.py`, `reckon/_store_section_ops.py` and `skills/reckon-edit/SKILL.md`, files §2, §5, §6 and §7 also write, and the driving followup orders only "§4 to §7".

findings.reason: it must be split or, as §7 was answered, each surface given its own verdict and negative control before a reviewer can close it on evidence.
findings.text: §5's title and deliverable carry four independent surfaces — `followups.<id>.title`/`.body`, `section_depends_on.<sid>`, `gates.<id>.measure`/`.required_evidence`, and the null-removes-a-key rule over four key kinds — with one test file and one done-when, so the node cannot be reviewed or closed on one verdict and its gate proves none of the four singly.

findings.reason: without a control the followup-text refusal (a resolved followup is a record and is refused) and the open-gate check can pass on code that never fires them, so the section's own measure rests on a suite that may be green on the unfixed handler.
findings.text: §5's done-when names two negative controls (a null `section_declarations.<id>` while its heading exists, a ref outside the grammar) for four surfaced paths, leaving the `followups.<id>.title`/`.body` path and the `gates.<id>.measure`/`.required_evidence` path with no declared control.
